hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes [IsPrincipalIdealRing O] as well. Mathlib has the instance `PrincipalIdealRing.isNoetherianRing` (Mathlib/RingTheory/PrincipalIdealDomain.lean, line 115). It only needs `[Semiring R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]` and gives `IsNoetherianRing R`. So if `[IsNoetherianRing O]` is omitted, the instance argument needed by `IPtHyp`, `ES` and `CSub` in the statement (all defined in the `Integral` section, which has the same variable block) is still found by instance search. `IsNoetherianRing` is a `Prop`-valued class, so by proof irrelevance the synthesized instance is definitionally equal to the omitted one. The statement therefore elaborates to the same thing. The proof (`rw [β, Equiv.trans_apply, AlgEquiv.arrowCongr_apply, liftSEquiv_apply]; rfl`) only unfolds definitions and goes through unchanged. No degenerate case is affected, because this is just a redundant instance.
